access.access.by-default-dsh-web-listens: By default dsh web listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and that is deliberate: it has no user system, so whoever can reach it is you. Choosing an access method is therefore really about how wide you want to open that door. The three methods below are ordered from smallest exposure to largest, and all assume the server has its own public IP.
access.access.how-to-actually-use-a-serv: How to actually use a server-side dsh web from your laptop and your phone
access.chooser.daily-use-several-devices: Daily use, several devices, home-screen app
access.chooser.for-yourself-only-take-fo: For yourself only, take ①. For long-term use with the least friction, take ③. Treat ② as a way to take a quick look.
access.chooser.just-you-one-or-two-devic: Just you, one or two devices
access.chooser.needs-a-domain-certificat: Needs a domain; certificates to maintain (certbot automates it)
access.chooser.showing-it-to-someone-bri: Showing it to someone briefly, no domain
access.chooser.token-travels-in-the-clea: token travels in the clear; some web APIs are unavailable
access.chooser.two-questions-decide-it-w: Two questions decide it: who needs access, and are you willing to open a port.
access.chooser.you-must-bring-the-tunnel: You must bring the tunnel up; phones need an SSH app
access.description: Three ways to reach a server-side DeepSeek Harness web from a laptop or phone: an SSH tunnel, an nginx reverse proxy without a domain, and nginx with a domain and TLS. Includes firewalls, --trusted-host and troubleshooting.
access.footer.note: Replace SERVER_IP, the domain and the token with your own
access.mobile.a-phone-browser-has-no-ter: A phone browser has no terminal, so method ① needs an SSH app while ② and ③ need nothing but a browser.
access.mobile.a-standalone-window-has-no: A standalone window has no address bar and feels closer to a native app — but note that iOS soft-keyboard behaviour differs slightly from a browser tab
access.mobile.add-it-to-the-home-screen-: Add it to the home screen
access.mobile.authenticate-once-use-it-f: Authenticate once, use it for a while
access.mobile.ios-safari-share-add-to-ho: iOS Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen. Android Chrome: menu → Add to Home screen / Install app
access.mobile.keep-the-token-link-in-a-p: Keep the token link in a password manager rather than in browser history
access.mobile.on-a-phone-how-each-method: On a phone: how each method feels
access.mobile.opening-the-token-link-aga: Opening the token link again buys another day
access.mobile.the-browser-only-allows-cl: The browser only allows clipboard writes over https — one more reason method ③ is the practical one
access.mobile.the-session-cookie-lasts-a: the session cookie lasts a day
access.mobile.what-makes-it-pleasant-on-: What makes it pleasant on a phone
access.mobile.with-the-dsh-mobile-ux-plu: With the dsh-mobile-ux plugin installed, the narrow layout, soft-keyboard tracking and single-tap session switching are already handled
access.nginx-domain.a-free-domain-plus-a: A free domain plus a Let's Encrypt certificate: no browser warnings, and on a phone you can add it to the home screen and use it like an app.
access.nginx-domain.add-an-a-record-host: Add an A record: host dsh, value = the server's public IP. Use @ for the apex if nothing else is there
access.nginx-domain.at-this-point-the-la: At this point the laptop and the phone use one address, the certificate is trusted, and the token stops appearing in everyday URLs (the session cookie covers a day).
access.nginx-domain.if-you-would-rather-: If you would rather control the config, issue with acme.sh in webroot mode and write the 443 site yourself:

If you would rather not manage certificates or a firewall, Cloudflare Tunnel is the alternative: run cloudflared on the server, point a tunnel at 127.0.0.1:3081, open no ports on the public side, and let Cloudflare terminate TLS. The cost is one external dependency — and the same --trusted-host entry for the domain.
access.nginx-domain.issue-a-certificate-: Issue a certificate and move nginx to 443
access.nginx-domain.issue-rewrite-the-co: # issue, rewrite the config, schedule renewal
access.nginx-domain.nginx-domain-tls-the: ③ nginx + domain + TLS: the one to live with
access.nginx-domain.no-domain-yet-free-s: No domain yet? Free subdomains work, e.g. DuckDNS or afraid.org's FreeDNS, or buy the cheapest TLD
access.nginx-domain.optional-an-extra-ba: # optional: an extra basic-auth gate (stacks with dsh's token prompt)
access.nginx-domain.point-a-domain-at-th: Point a domain at the server
access.nginx-domain.same-rule-as-method-: Same rule as method ②, with the domain on the allow-list instead of the IP:
access.nginx-domain.the-least-work-is-ce: The least work is certbot: it issues the certificate, rewrites the nginx config and installs automatic renewal.
access.nginx-domain.verify-before-going-: Verify before going on: dig +short dsh.example.com must return your public IP
access.nginx-ip.a-first-visit-with-the-t: # a first visit with the token passes; everything else needs the session cookie
access.nginx-ip.be-clear-about-the-cost-: Be clear about the cost of plain HTTP: the token appears in the URL (browser history, proxy logs), anyone on the path can read it, and http:// is not a secure context, so the browser restricts the clipboard and parts of the PWA surface. Fine for a quick look; use ③ for anything long-lived.
access.nginx-ip.enable-the-site-and-open: Enable the site and open the port
access.nginx-ip.exactly-the-token-dsh-we: # exactly the token dsh web printed
access.nginx-ip.grab-the-token-and-open-: Grab the token and open it
access.nginx-ip.install-nginx-and-add-on: Install nginx and add one site
access.nginx-ip.nginx-reverse-proxy-publ: ② nginx reverse proxy: public IP, no domain
access.nginx-ip.on-a-cloud-vm-also-open-: On a cloud VM also open the same port in the console's security group; forgetting it looks exactly like “works from the box, unreachable from outside”
access.nginx-ip.serve-it-directly-from-t: Serve it directly from the server and open http://IP:port. Minimal configuration, at the cost of plain HTTP and a token that travels in the URL.
access.nginx-ip.that-if-block-is-only-a-: That if block is only a placeholder: dsh's own token cookie is the access control, and nginx just forwards. For an extra gate, the basic auth or Cloudflare Tunnel in ③ is less trouble.
access.nginx-ip.when-you-reach-it-by-ip-: When you reach it by IP the browser's Host header is that IP, and dsh web only serves /api/* to allow-listed hosts, so add it explicitly:
access.prereq.401-is-normal-no-token-no-: # 401 is normal: no token, no entry
access.prereq.an-elastic-or-static-ip-fr: An elastic or static IP from the cloud console counts; a private IP or one behind carrier NAT does not
access.prereq.check-with-curl-s-ifconfig: Check with: curl -s ifconfig.me — the address it prints must match the console
access.prereq.dsh-web-only-accepts-host-: dsh web only accepts host names on the --trusted-host allow-list; anything else gets 403 on /api/*
access.prereq.every-launch-prints-an-acc: Every launch prints an access link containing a token — keep it handy
access.prereq.four-things-every-method-r: Four things every method relies on. Confirming them first saves most of the debugging later.
access.prereq.know-who-the-host-header-i: Know who the Host header is
access.prereq.method-tunnels-over-ssh-so: Method ① tunnels over SSH, so this has to work first
access.prereq.methods-and-need-it-to-ins: Methods ② and ③ need it to install nginx and issue certificates
access.prereq.reaching-it-by-ip-means-li: Reaching it by IP means listing the IP; by domain means listing the domain. https does not make a host trusted by itself
access.prereq.required-by-and-not-by-4: Required by ② and ③; not by ①
access.prereq.the-server-has-its-own-pub: The server has its own public IP
access.prereq.the-token-link-is-printed-: # the token link is printed here
access.prereq.the-unit-is-called-dsh-web: The unit is called dsh-web below; what matters is that you can restart it and read its logs
access.title: Access guide — reach a server-side dsh web from a laptop or a phone
access.trouble.bundle-revisions-come-fro: Bundle revisions come from file mtime/size and are cached immutably — restart dsh-web so the URL changes
access.trouble.curl-works-on-the-box-not: curl works on the box, nothing from outside
access.trouble.it-works-but-streamed-out: It works, but streamed output stalls
access.trouble.local-port-taken-or-the-f: Local port taken; or the forward targets the server's public IP instead of 127.0.0.1
access.trouble.nginx-buffering-or-timeou: nginx buffering or timeout: add proxy_buffering off and a longer proxy_read_timeout
access.trouble.opened-without-the-token-: Opened without the token, or the day-long cookie expired
access.trouble.plugin-code-changed-brows: Plugin code changed, browser shows the old behaviour
access.trouble.the-cloud-security-group-: The cloud security group or the host firewall has not been opened
access.trouble.the-host-is-not-on-truste: The Host is not on --trusted-host, so /api/* returns 403
access.trouble.the-page-loads-but-the-ui: The page loads, but the UI errors or stays blank
access.trouble.the-tunnel-is-up-but-the-: The tunnel is up but the browser cannot connect
access.trouble.these-cover-most-of-the-i: These cover most of the “it does not connect” cases.
access.tunnel.a-phone-browser-cannot-ope: A phone browser cannot open a tunnel by itself, so an SSH app on the phone has to do it:
access.tunnel.after-that-ssh-n-dsh-is-en: After that, ssh -N dsh is enough — the forward lives in the config
access.tunnel.for-automatic-reconnect-in: For automatic reconnect, install autossh: autossh -M 0 -N dsh
access.tunnel.forward-the-server-s-127-0: Forward the server's 127.0.0.1:3081 to your own machine over SSH. Traffic is encrypted end to end and no extra port is opened on the server — start here.
access.tunnel.get-the-full-token-link-fi: Get the full token link first
access.tunnel.if-local-3081-is-taken-use: If local 3081 is taken, use -L 8080:127.0.0.1:3081 instead
access.tunnel.ios-termius-the-free-tier-: iOS: Termius (the free tier is enough) or similar; add a local port forward 3081 → 127.0.0.1:3081 to the connection
access.tunnel.l-3081-127-0-0-1-3081-loca: -L 3081:127.0.0.1:3081: local port 3081 to the server's 127.0.0.1:3081, through SSH
access.tunnel.make-it-nicer-alias-and-au: Make it nicer: alias and auto-reconnect
access.tunnel.n-forward-only-without-ope: -N: forward only, without opening an interactive shell on the server
access.tunnel.nothing-needs-to-change-in: Nothing needs to change in --trusted-host here: the request's Host is 127.0.0.1:3081, which is already allowed. That is why this method is the least work.
access.tunnel.open-a-tunnel-from-your-la: Open a tunnel from your laptop
access.tunnel.run-this-on-the-server-the: Run this on the server; the token printed by dsh web is the launch token.
access.tunnel.serveraliveinterval-keeps-: ServerAliveInterval keeps an idle tunnel alive through middleboxes
access.tunnel.some-clients-drop-the-tunn: Some clients drop the tunnel when backgrounded; allow the app to stay resident
access.tunnel.swap-the-host-for-127-0-0-: Swap the host for 127.0.0.1 and open it
access.tunnel.the-first-visit-with-the-t: The first visit with the token plants a session cookie, after which http://127.0.0.1:3081 just works.
access.tunnel.then-browse-to-http-127-0-: Then browse to http://127.0.0.1:3081 on the phone — that 127.0.0.1 is the phone itself
access.tunnel.to-let-other-devices-on-th: To let other devices on the same LAN (a tablet, say) ride the tunnel, the forward has to listen on 0.0.0.0: set GatewayPorts clientspecified on the server and add -g to the command. That publishes port 3081 to your local network — only do it temporarily, on a network you trust.
access.tunnel.want-the-tunnel-on-a-phone: Want the tunnel on a phone too?
index.credits.an-alternative-approach-to: An alternative approach to the phone tier (breakpoint layer, state bridge, data-slot stylesheet); its trade-offs informed ours, MIT
index.credits.another-take-on-the-same-c: Another take on the same class of problems; useful on install and troubleshooting
index.credits.the-1-styles-and-the-3-tap: The §1 styles and the §3 tap-outside collapse logic come directly from dsh-web-mobile-fix (MIT); this repo merges and corrects them. §2 had nothing to copy from — every constant in it comes from measurements on one device.
index.credits.the-1-styles-and-the-tap-o: The §1 styles and the tap-outside-to-collapse behaviour come from upstream; §2 was ground out against a real phone.
index.credits.the-original-1-implementat: The original §1 implementation (settings panel, floating sidebar, scrim, tap-outside collapse), MIT
index.credits.the-shell-being-adapted-th: The shell being adapted; the plugin anchors only on its data-slot and class-prefix contracts
index.description: A mobile-first UX pack for the DeepSeek Harness web shell: narrow-screen layout fixes, iOS keyboard and composer handling, single-tap session switching, and a trajectory panel that opens on its newest entry. Client-side only, no desktop regressions, every section individually switchable.
index.features.a-double-click-inside-600: A double click inside 600ms is swallowed, so rename no longer fires by accident
index.features.a-few-follow-up-measureme: A few follow-up measurements after the keyboard settles remove the empty band
index.features.built-and-switched-sectio: Built and switched section by section: a phone is the only place any of it can be judged.
index.features.composer-tracks-the-keybo: Composer tracks the keyboard: the shell is pinned to visualViewport.height and always floored, since one extra pixel makes the document scrollable again
index.features.focus-zoom-guard-editable: Focus-zoom guard: editables are raised to 17px in a stylesheet — iOS decides whether to zoom the moment focus moves, so writing it in a focus handler is already too late for the first tap
index.features.it-reuses-the-product-s-o: It reuses the product's own open handler instead of reimplementing session semantics
index.features.one-tap-switches-immediat: One tap switches immediately, without waiting out a double-tap window
index.features.settings-becomes-a-full-s: Settings becomes a full-screen column with a horizontally scrollable tab row
index.features.tapping-outside-the-drawe: Tapping outside the drawer collapses it
index.features.the-composer-bar-stops-wr: The composer bar stops wrapping: the tool cluster shrinks, the send button does not
index.features.the-document-is-scroll-lo: The document is scroll-locked while the keyboard is up
index.features.the-drawer-collapses-afte: The drawer collapses afterwards, by pressing its own toggle button so the shell's real code path runs
index.features.the-sidebar-floats-over-t: The sidebar floats over the conversation while the grid keeps its 56px rail
index.features.touch-narrow-screens-desk: Touch + narrow screens; desktop double-click rename is untouched
index.features.touch-surfaces-while-an-e: Touch surfaces, while an editable is focused
index.footer.note: Built for the DeepSeek Harness web profile
index.index.a-plugin-change-needs-a-rest: # A plugin change needs a restart, or the browser keeps running the old code (immutable cache)
index.index.make-the-deepseek-harness-we: Make the DeepSeek Harness web UI genuinely usable on a phone
index.index.one-client-side-plugin-that-: One client-side plugin that fixes narrow-screen layout, iOS keyboard and composer tracking, and single-tap session switching: no shell source changes, no desktop regression, and every section can be switched off on its own.
index.index.tuned-against-a-real-iphone-: Tuned against a real iPhone + Safari
index.install.dsh-derives-each-bundle-re: DSH derives each bundle revision from the file's mtime/ctime/size, and the response is cached as immutable for a year. Without a restart the file is new and the server serves it, yet the browser still runs the old code — a trap that has caused several wrong conclusions.
index.install.hard-refresh-the-page-on-t: Hard-refresh the page on the phone (pull to refresh in Safari), then check each item:
index.install.or-your-own-dsh-web-proces: # or your own dsh web process
index.install.requires-node-22-and-a-dsh: Requires Node ≥ 22 and a DSH web profile.
index.install.settings-opens-as-a-full-s: Settings opens as a full-screen column with scrollable tabs
index.install.tap-an-unselected-session-: Tap an unselected session: one tap switches to it and the drawer collapses
index.install.tap-the-composer-the-page-: Tap the composer: the page must not zoom. Type or backspace: the composer must not drop
index.install.tap-the-top-left-icon-the-: Tap the top-left icon: the sidebar should float over the conversation, and tapping outside collapses it
index.install.the-composer-buttons-stay-: The composer buttons stay on one row, with no wrapping or overlap
index.limits.3-only-handles-the-sidebar-: §3 only handles the sidebar session list; search-result sessions use different markup and are not covered yet.
index.limits.no-product-source-is-modifi: No product source is modified and no server component is required; removing the plugin is fully reversible.
index.limits.selectors-anchor-on-the-pro: Selectors anchor on the product's data-slot attributes and CSS-Module class prefixes. Stable within a release line, but a major product revamp may need small updates.
index.limits.the-focus-zoom-guard-overri: The focus-zoom guard overrides the content font size: on a phone the editor is fixed at 17px, so the “small” setting no longer applies to it. Dropping back to 14px brings the zoom right back — a trade-off, not an oversight.
index.switches.allow-or-forbid-magnifica: Allow or forbid magnification. The scale is pinned by default (maximum-scale=1), the only way to stop the iOS focus-zoom; the price is that pinch zoom goes too
index.switches.append-a-comma-separated-: Append a comma-separated list to ?dshMobileUx=, or override before load with window.__dshMobileUxOptions = { keyboard: false }. Note the …Options suffix: the readout API lives on window.__dshMobileUx, and neither overwrites the other.
index.switches.do-not-scroll-lock-the-do: Do not scroll-lock the document while the keyboard is up
index.switches.dshmobileux-tap-means-onl: ?dshMobileUx=tap means "only single-tap switching" and turns the keyboard follower off with everything else; to remove one section use no<name>. hud, lock and zoom are modifiers and never take part in a keep-list.
index.switches.keep-only-the-listed-sect: Keep only the listed sections (the keep-list is exclusive; see the note below)
index.switches.leave-the-drawer-open-aft: Leave the drawer open after a tap
index.switches.show-the-live-readout-in-: Show the live readout in the top-left corner: vvH / root / kb / lock / y / oT
index.title: dsh-mobile-ux — a mobile UX pack for the DSH Web shell
index.why.a-band-of-empty-space-is-left-: A band of empty space is left between the composer and the keyboard
index.why.after-typing-or-a-backspace-th: After typing or a backspace the composer drops behind the keyboard
index.why.all-of-them-came-from-actually: All of them came from actually using this on a phone, not from taste.
index.why.composer-buttons-wrap-and-over: Composer buttons wrap and overlap each other
index.why.opening-the-sidebar-squeezes-t: Opening the sidebar squeezes the conversation to roughly 110px
index.why.switching-sessions-needs-two-t: Switching sessions needs two taps, and a fast double tap renames instead
index.why.tapping-the-composer-zooms-the: Tapping the composer zooms the whole page and hides the input
index.why.the-composer-is-laid-out-for-a: The composer is laid out for a desktop width
index.why.the-editor-renders-at-14px-and: The editor renders at 14px, and iOS zooms the page for any focused editable under 16px
index.why.the-height-is-measured-before-: The height is measured before the keyboard animation settles and no later event corrects it
index.why.the-row-opens-on-click-but-ren: The row opens on click, but rename hangs off a double click on the title inside it, so the second tap reads as a double click
index.why.the-settings-dialog-is-squeeze: The settings dialog is squeezed to a sliver and its tabs stack into a column
index.why.the-shell-has-no-phone-tier-be: The shell has no phone tier below 768px
index.why.the-shell-is-as-tall-as-the-la: The shell is as tall as the layout viewport, but an overlay keyboard only shrinks the visual viewport; the page becomes scrollable and the browser scrolls the composer away
index.why.the-sidebar-is-a-grid-column-r: The sidebar is a grid column rather than an overlay
install.description: How to install dsh-mobile-ux into a DSH web profile from GitHub, npm or a local directory, with three levels of verification, the section switches, uninstall and upgrade, and install-time troubleshooting.
install.footer.note: Replace the profile name with your own
install.github.a-home-screen-standalone-: A home-screen standalone window: swipe it away and reopen
install.github.installing-without-restar: Installing without restarting looks like nothing happened: DSH derives bundle revisions from file mtime/ctime/size and caches responses as immutable for a year, so the browser keeps running the old code.
install.github.iphone-safari-pull-to-ref: iPhone Safari: pull to refresh, or close the tab and reopen
install.github.method-a-install-straight: Method A: install straight from GitHub (recommended)
install.github.no-npm-publish-and-no-man: No npm publish and no manual copying required. Verified end to end.
install.github.pnpm-fetches-the-repo-and: pnpm fetches the repo and registers it in the profile's dependencies and dsh.profile.bundles
install.github.to-follow-new-commits-on-: To follow new commits on main, run dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-mobile-ux
install.github.to-pin-a-revision-use-git: To pin a revision, use github:68110923/dsh-mobile-ux#v2.0.0 once a tag exists
install.install.install-this-plugin-on-y: Install this plugin on your own DSH
install.install.one-command-no-build-ste: One command. No build step, no server component, no product source changes. Restart dsh web and refresh; removing it is one command too.
install.local.a-directory-install-is-a-s: A directory install is a symlink: edit the source, restart dsh-web, done
install.local.copy-the-repo-onto-the-ser: Copy the repo onto the server
install.local.for-a-fully-offline-box-np: For a fully offline box, npm pack elsewhere and install the resulting tgz
install.local.install-from-the-directory: Install from the directory and restart
install.local.method-c-local-directory-o: Method C: local directory or offline
install.local.use-this-when-github-is-no: Use this when GitHub is not an option or the machine has no outbound network.
install.npm.method-b-install-from-npm-no: Method B: install from npm (not available yet)
install.npm.on-a-registry-mirror-a-fresh: On a registry mirror a fresh version may not be synced; add --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
install.npm.once-published-it-will-look-: Once published, it will look like this
install.npm.the-name-will-carry-the-publ: The name will carry the publisher's scope; installing is faster than GitHub and does not depend on GitHub being reachable
install.npm.the-publisher-s-npm-account-: The publisher's npm account uses a security-key form of 2FA (Auth & Writes) while this server has no TOTP authenticator, and npm demands an OTP — or a 2FA-bypassing token — for publishing. Three attempts (granular token, unscoped package, organization scope) were all rejected by the registry.
install.npm.this-package-is-not-on-npm-y: This package is not on npm yet. Below is how it will work once it is, and what is blocking it today.
install.npm.to-publish-later-github-acti: To publish later, GitHub Actions with Trusted Publishing (OIDC) sidesteps both tokens and OTPs
install.npm.users-are-unaffected-method-: Users are unaffected: method A installs the very same package, verified byte for byte
install.req.a-dsh-cli-that-can-boot-a-we: A dsh CLI that can boot a web profile
install.req.a-github-install-needs-git-o: a github: install needs git over HTTPS
install.req.a-registry-mirror-can-stall-: A registry mirror can stall a GitHub dependency; point at the official registry if needed
install.req.a-spawn-pnpm-enoent-error-me: A spawn pnpm ENOENT error means dsh's bin directory is not on PATH
install.req.dsh-plugin-delegates-to-pnpm: dsh plugin delegates to pnpm, provided by dsh's own runtime
install.req.network-access-to-github-or-: Network access to GitHub or npm
install.req.on-an-offline-box-clone-the-: On an offline box, clone the repo elsewhere and use method C
install.req.plugins-install-into-a-profi: Plugins install into a profile, so that profile has to boot first
install.req.tested-on-dsh-0-1-7-rc-1-oth: Tested on DSH 0.1.7-rc.1; other 0.1.x releases are expected to work
install.req.the-examples-use-the-profile: The examples use the profile name web; substitute your own if it differs.
install.req.three-checks-fix-any-that-fa: Three checks. Fix any that fail before installing.
install.switches.allow-magnification-by-: Allow magnification (by default the scale is pinned so focus cannot magnify the page)
install.switches.disable-the-whole-pack-: Disable the whole pack for that page load, without uninstalling
install.switches.it-works-as-is-these-ar: It works as-is. These are the two switches people reach for; the full list is on the home page.
install.switches.keep-everything-except-: Keep everything except single-tap session switching
install.switches.live-readout-in-the-cor: Live readout in the corner, for debugging
install.switches.modifiers-such-as-hud-n: Modifiers such as hud never count as a section in a keep-list
install.switches.not-all-of-it-turn-sect: Not all of it? Turn sections off
install.switches.turn-off-the-keyboard-f: Turn off the keyboard follower and the scroll lock, keeping the rest
install.title: Install guide — put dsh-mobile-ux on your own DSH
install.trouble.almost-always-a-missing-: Almost always a missing dsh-web restart or a page that was not hard-refreshed (immutable cache).
install.trouble.apply-threw-at-runtime-t: apply() threw at runtime — this is not a dependency problem. Read the stack in journalctl -u dsh-web against client.js.
install.trouble.dsh-cannot-find-its-bund: dsh cannot find its bundled pnpm. Put dsh's bin directory on PATH and retry.
install.trouble.no-route-to-github-use-t: No route to GitHub: use the npm method, or method C from a local directory.
install.trouble.remember-that-cordis-cli: Remember that cordis' client Context is a Proxy: reaching for an undeclared service throws instead of returning undefined. Use ctx.get() for optional lookups, and never assume a service such as ctx.styles exists.
install.trouble.the-bundle-could-not-be-: The bundle could not be resolved from the profile's node_modules: confirm it is installed into that same profile, then restart dsh web.
install.trouble.the-package-is-not-on-np: The package is not on npm yet (see method B); use method A from GitHub.
install.trouble.the-plugin-shows-as-fail: The plugin shows as failed in settings
install.uninstall.fully-reversible-the-p: Fully reversible: the plugin only injects styles, listeners and a few inline properties, and removes them all on unload.
install.uninstall.use-update-add-does-no: use update; add does not upgrade
install.uninstall.why-add-is-not-enough-: Why add is not enough: a git-installed package is pinned to one commit. On a second add, pnpm sees an unchanged specifier, prints “Lockfile is up to date, resolution step is skipped” and stops — not a byte changes. update re-resolves the dependency and fetches the newest commit.
install.verify.by-eye-which-is-fastest-o: By eye, which is fastest on a phone
install.verify.for-a-live-readout-append: For a live readout, append ?dshMobileUx=hud to the page URL: vvH / root / kb / lock appear in the corner, and a phone screenshot is enough to diagnose.
install.verify.layer-1-the-package-is-in: Layer 1: the package is in the profile
install.verify.layer-2-the-server-can-re: Layer 2: the server can resolve it (the step people skip)
install.verify.open-the-console-on-the-i: Open the console on the instrumented page (Safari's inspector, or prefix an address-bar snippet with javascript:) and run:
install.verify.tapping-an-unselected-ses: Tapping an unselected session switches in one tap and collapses the drawer
install.verify.tapping-the-composer-does: Tapping the composer does not zoom; typing and backspace keep it above the keyboard
install.verify.the-composer-buttons-stay: The composer buttons stay on one row; settings is a full-screen column
install.verify.the-sidebar-floats-over-t: The sidebar floats over the conversation with a scrim; tapping outside collapses it
install.verify.three-layers-it-is-instal: Three layers: it is installed, the server resolved it, and the browser is actually running it.
